s01-hook.recognized: When someone is in danger in the United States there's one number almost everyone knows

s02-questions.recognized: But why is it 911 Who created it What did Americans do before 911 existed And perhaps most interestinglyâ€

s03-911-vs-911.recognized: Was the emergency number actually named because of the terrorist attacks of September 11

s04-answer.recognized: The answer is no In fact 911 existed for more than three decades before 9/11

s05-origin.recognized: The story of 911 begins in the 1960s

s06-local-numbers.recognized: Back then there was no single emergency number covering the United States If you needed the police fire department or an ambulance you generally had to know and dial the local telephone number for the appropriate service And that created a serious problem

s07-every-second.recognized: Imagine witnessing a serious accident Someone is injured There's a fire And you have to stop and figure out which number to call Every second matters

s08-britain-999.recognized: The idea of a single emergency number wasn't completely new In fact Britain had already introduced nine-nine-nine as an emergency number in 1937

s09-momentum.recognized: In the United States the idea gained momentum during the 1950s and 1960s In 1967 the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice recommended creating a single number for reporting emergencies The Federal Communications Commission then worked with AT&T to find a number that could be implemented across the country

s10-why-911.recognized: So why did they choose 911 AT&T selected the number because it was short easy to remember andâ€ criticallyâ€ had not already been assigned as an area code office code or service code in the telephone system

s11-rotary.recognized: It also fit the technology of the time Remember these were the days of rotary phones The number needed to be simple enough to remember and quick enough to dial during an emergency

s12-operator.recognized: Before 911 one common option was to dial 0 and reach a telephone operator The operator could then help connect the caller to the appropriate emergency service

s13-not-dedicated.recognized: But this wasn't a dedicated emergency system It depended on the operator local telephone infrastructure and knowing where the appropriate emergency service was

s14-fire-chiefs.recognized: As emergency calls increased and society became more dependent on telephones the limitations became increasingly obvious Fire officials had already been pushing for a simpler emergency number In 1957 the National Association of Fire Chiefs reportedly recommended a single number for reporting fires

s16-haleyville.recognized: Then came February 16th, 1968 In Haleyville, Alabama something happened that would eventually change emergency communications across America

s17-first-call.recognized: Alabama Speaker of the House Rankin Fite picked up a telephone and dialed 911 The call was answered by U.S. Representative Tom Bevill at the local police station It was the first official 911 call in the United States

s18-rollout.recognized: But here's something important 911 didn't instantly become available everywhere in America The system took years to expand Different communities and telephone companies had to build the infrastructure necessary to route emergency calls Eventually 911 became the standard Americans know today

s19-what-prompted.recognized: So what actually prompted the creation of 911 There wasn't one single event It was the growing realization that emergency communication needed to become faster simpler and more reliable

s20-nas-report.recognized: The United States was experiencing growing numbers of emergencies including serious injuries from automobile crashes A landmark 1966 report from the National Academy of Sciences highlighted accidental death and injury as a major public-health problem and called for exploring a single nationwide telephone number to summon an ambulance

s21-communication.recognized: At the same time police and fire officials were pushing for simpler ways for the public to report emergencies In other wordsâ€

s22-atlantic.recognized: Now let's cross the Atlantic The United States uses 911 The United Kingdom uses nine-nine-nine So are they basically the same thing In purpose yes Both are emergency numbers designed to connect people with emergency services But they are different numbers belonging to different national telephone systems

s23-uk-112.recognized: And here's another interesting fact The UK also supports one-one-two the pan-European emergency number So if you're in Britain you don't normally dial 911 You dial nine-nine-nine or one-one-two for emergencies

s24-london.recognized: So if an American tourist in London instinctively dials 911â€ That's not the number they should rely on

s25-confusion.recognized: Now for one of the biggest misconceptions surrounding 911 Some people assume the emergency number was created because of the September 11 terrorist attacks But look at the dates

s26-dates.recognized: The first 911 call happened in 1968 The September 11 attacks happened in 2001 That's a difference of 33 years

s27-coincidence.recognized: So there is no causal connection between the terrorist attacks and the creation of the 911 emergency number The similarity is simply a coincidence

s28-where-911.recognized: So is 911 only used in the United States No. A number of countries and territories use 911 as an emergency number either as their primary emergency number or alongside other numbers Examples include Canada Mexico the Philippines American Samoa Antigua and Barbuda and several Caribbean countries

s29-warning.recognized: But there's an important warning Don't assume that 911 works everywhere just because it works in the United States Emergency numbers vary dramatically around the world

s30-world-numbers.recognized: And some countries support multiple emergency numbers For example the United Kingdom uses nine-nine-nine and one-one-two Here are some important emergency numbers you may encounter around the world

s31-travel.recognized: And this is why travelers should check the local emergency number before visiting another country The number that saves a life in one country might do absolutely nothing in another

s32-one-number.recognized: One of the biggest advantages of systems like 911 is that you don't necessarily have to know which emergency service you need You explain what is happening The call-taker can determine what kind of response is required and dispatch the appropriate emergency services

s33-real-power.recognized: That's the real power of a universal emergency number It's not just about remembering three digits It's about removing a decision from someone who may already be panicking

s35-three-digits.recognized: Three digits Easy to remember Easy to dial And in the right situationâ€

s36-end.recognized: â€ those three digits can be the difference between waiting for helpâ€ and getting it
